title: Focused Ion Beam Lithography to Etch Nano-architectures into Microelectrodes
protocol: Mount Non-functional Silicon Probe for Focused Ion Beam (FIB) Lithography while wearing proper personal protective equipment, such as a lab coat and gloves.
Isolate a strip of 2-3 silicon probes from the silicon on insulator (SOI) wafer containing 1,000 probes using fine forceps while wearing gloves.
Clean the isolated silicon probe thoroughly to remove all dust and debris prior to FIB etching.
Prepare a 6 well polystyrene plate by pipetting 3 mL/well of 95% ethanol into three wells.
Carefully pick up the cut strip of silicon probes using fine tip or vacuum forceps.
Place the strip into cell strainer, ensuring only one strip per strainer.
Immerse the strainer in the first well containing 95% ethanol for cleaning.
Keep the strainer in the first well for 5 min.
Move the strainer to the second well with 95% ethanol and clean for another 5 min.
Repeat the cleaning step once more in the third well.
Place the cleaned silicon probes on a polytetrafluoroethylene plate to air dry.
Perform this step in a sterile hood to avoid contamination from dust.
After drying, place the strip of silicon probes in a sealed container for transport to the SEM-FIB.
Wrap the strainer containing the air-dried samples with plastic or aluminum foil for transport and/or storage.
Use a toothpick to place a tiny drop (~10 µL) of silver paint on the edge of the silicon substrate surrounding the probes.
Spread the silver paint around the sides of the silicon substrate to secure the strip down.
Allow the silver paint to dry completely before placing the aluminum stub into the SEM-FIB.
Move the stage to coordinates X = 70 mm, Y = 70 mm, Z = 0 mm, T = 0°, R = 0°.
Vent the chamber.
Put on clean nitrile gloves.
Open the chamber door.
Unscrew the central bolt counterclockwise to remove the stage adapter if necessary.
Install a new stage adapter by screwing it clockwise into the rotation plate of the stage.
Insert the aluminum stub holding the probes into the top of the stage adapter.
Tighten the set screw on the side of the stage adapter using a 1.5 mm hex wrench.
Turn the adapter clockwise to lower its height or counterclockwise to raise it as needed.
Secure the stage adapter to the rotation plate by turning the locking cone nut clockwise until it is secure against the stage rotation plate.
Hold the stage adapter with one hand to prevent rotation while tightening the locking cone nut.
Use the provided height gauge to ensure the top of the aluminum stub aligns with the maximum line on the gauge.
Do not over tighten the cone nut to avoid damaging the stage and adapter.
Acquire a navigation camera image.
Carefully swing the navigation camera arm open until it stops.
Watch the live image in Quadrant 3 of the microscope user interface (UI).
Wait for the brightness level to auto adjust appropriately.
Push the button down on the camera bracket to acquire the image.
Ensure the entire image acquisition finishes, indicated by a pause symbol and the illumination turning off.
Swing the camera arm back to the closed position.
Carefully close the microscope chamber door.
Watch the CCD camera image in Quadrant 4 while closing the door.
Ensure that samples and stage are safely away from critical components.
Select the down arrow next to the Pump button in the beam control tab.
Select Pump with Sample Cleaning button in the UI software to start the chamber vacuum pump and built-in plasma cleaner.
Gently push on the face of the door while the pump is running to ensure it is sealed.
Wait for approximately 8 minutes for the pumping time and plasma cleaning cycle to complete.
Press the Wake-Up button in the beam control tab to turn on the electron and ion beams.
Select quadrant 1 and set the beam signal to electron beam.
Set quadrant 2 to ion beam.
Set SEM voltage to 5 kV.
Set SEM beam current to 0.20 nA.
Set SEM detector to ETD.
Set detector mode to Secondary Electron.
Set FIB voltage to 30 kV.
Set FIB beam current to 24 pA.
Set FIB detector to ICE detector.
Set detector mode to the secondary electron.
Double click on the silicon probe in the navigation camera image, quadrant 3 to move the stage to the approximate location of the probe.
Click on quadrant 1 to select it as the active quadrant and hit the pause button to start SEM scanning.
Set the scan dwell time to 300 ns.
Turn off scan interlacing.
Turn off line integration.
Turn off frame averaging.
Set scan rotation to 0 in the beam control tab.
Right click on the beam shift 2d adjuster and select zero.
Adjust the magnification to the minimum value by turning the magnification knob counterclockwise on the MUI panel.
Adjust the image brightness using the knobs on MUI panel or the Auto Contrast Brightness toolbar icon.
Adjust the image contrast using the knobs on MUI panel or the Auto Contrast Brightness toolbar icon.
Double-left-click the mouse on a feature to center it in the SEM image or press down the mouse wheel and activate joystick mouse mode.
Move the desired silicon probe into the center of the SEM image.
Locate an edge or other features such as a dust particle or scratch.
Increase magnification to 2,000x by turning the magnification knob clockwise.
Adjust the focus of the SEM by turning the coarse and fine focus knobs until the image is in focus.
Select the Link sample Z to working distance button in the toolbar.
Type in 4.0 mm in the Z axis position and push the Go To button or hit enter key to move the stage to 4 mm working distance.
Move the stage in X and Y to locate the shoulder of the silicon probe.
Position the shoulder as close to the center of the SEM image as possible.
Change the stage tilt to 52˚ by typing in "52" in the T coordinate and hitting enter.
Use the Stage Z slider to bring the shoulder of the probe back to the center of the SEM image, adjusting only the Z position.
Run the built-in "xT Align Feature" command.
Click on two points parallel to the edge of the probe using the mouse.
Select the horizontal radio button in the popup window and click finish.
Adjust the stage in X,Y using the mouse to put the lower shoulder of the probe in the center of the SEM image again.
Select the FIB in quadrant 2.
Ensure the beam current is still 24 pA.
Set the magnification to 5,000x and the dwell time to 100 ns.
Type Ctrl-F on the keyboard to set the FIB focus to 13.0 mm.
Right-click in the stigmator 2d adjuster and select zero.
Right-click in the Beam Shift 2d adjuster and select zero.
Set the scan rotation to 0°.
Push the auto contrast brightness button in the toolbar.
Acquire an image of the probe shoulder in quadrant 2 using the snapshot tool.
Confirm the probe shoulder is in the center of the FIB image, if not, double-click on the probe shoulder to move it to center.
Move the stage to the left by pushing the left arrow key approximately 10-15 times.
Take another snapshot and observe whether the probe side is still in the center of the FIB.
Start the Nanobuilder software from the Windows start menu.
Position the software window on the side monitor.
Open the file for patterning silicon probes by clicking File and then Open.
Direct the browser to Supplementary File 1 named "Case_Western_2000_micron_Final_11H47M_runtime.jbj".
Select Set stage origin from the microscope dropdown menu within the software.
Select Calibrate Detectors from the microscope dropdown menu in the software.
Click once on Quad 1 with the mouse to select it for calibration.
Start the calibration process by clicking OK.
Ensure ETD and ICE detectors calibrate successfully.
Choose Execute from the microscope dropdown menu to start the patterning sequence.
Close the software when the pattern is complete.
Hit "Vent" in the microscope UI beam control tab to shut down the microscope beams and start the vent cycle.
Move the stage to coordinates X = 70 mm, Y = 70 mm, Z = 0 mm, T = 0°, R = 0° while the chamber is venting.
Put on clean nitrile gloves once the chamber is vented.
Pull open the chamber door.
Loosen the set screw on the stub adapter using the 1.5 mm hex wrench.
Remove the aluminum stub containing the patterned probe from the chamber.
Carefully close the microscope chamber door.
Watch the CCD camera image in Quadrant 4 while closing the door to ensure that the stage adapter is a safe distance away from any critical component in the microscope chamber.
Select the down arrow next to the Pump button in the beam control tab.
Select Pump button to start the chamber vacuum pump.
Ensure the door is sealed by gently pushing on the face of the door while the pump is running.
Gently remove the functional silicon electrode from its packaging.
Use forceps to carefully lift the plastic protective tab covering the head stage.
Clamp the electrode with hemostats to prepare for mounting into the stereotaxic frame.
Hold the covered tab with the forceps and place curved hemostats around the green shaft above the silicon shank, with the curved part facing upwards towards the tab.
Lock the hemostats in place to ensure the electrode will not drop out of the hemostats.
Gently remove the plastic protective tab covering the head stage.
Hold the electrode with the hemostats and clip the electrode into the stereotaxic frame for cleaning.
Fill 3 Petri dishes with 95% ethanol (~10 mL per petri dish).
Place the Petri dish under the electrode that is mounted into the stereotaxic frame for cleaning.
Slowly lower the electrode by turning the micromanipulator downwards (100 µm/s) so that the shank is submerged into the 95% ethanol.
Leave the electrode shank in 95% ethanol for 5 min.
Slowly raise the electrode out of the 95% ethanol by turning the micromanipulator upwards at a rate of 100 µm/s.
Repeat the wash step two more times, for a total of three washes.
Allow the electrode to air dry for five minutes.
Mount the cleaned functional silicon electrode onto an aluminum stand.
Place the electrode shank on the aluminum stub so it does not hang over any edge.
Pin the headstage securely to the aluminum stub using a small piece of Cu or carbon conductive tape.
Position the electrode at the eucentric height and ensure it is at the coincidence point of the SEM and FIB beams.
Align the shank with the "X" direction of the stage.
Set the FIB to the optimal current for milling the required nano-architecture.
Correct the focus and stigmation settings.
Prepare an array of lines with desired spacing and length to cover the field of view of the shank (500 µm sections).
Adjust line lengths as etching progresses through thinner sections of the shank.
Check the milling quality before moving on to the next section after completing each section.
Align milled lines from previous sections to patterns used for the next section to prevent large gaps between runs.
